voices.name: Factual/reference
voices.description: Third-person, factual description of KORR's testing methodology and what differentiates it from consumer wearables. No hype, no superlatives beyond what the source material itself states (e.g. 'considered the gold standard').

voices.name: Reddit-safe mention (peer voice)
voices.description: When KORR is mentioned inside first-person, peer-voice content (e.g. someone describing a personal testing experience): mention once, then switch to pronouns ("it", "the system"); frame as "what I used", never as a recommendation; always acknowledge the tradeoff vs. wearable estimates.
voices.best_for: Any first-person/community content referencing a KORR test result

reddit_safe_mention.pattern_example: I got tested at a lab that uses breath-by-breath analysis (KORR system). It showed 52 ml/kg/min, while my Garmin had estimated 48. The difference makes sense since one measures and one estimates, but...
rules: Mention the brand once, then use pronouns
Never repeat the brand name unnecessarily
Never make a direct recommendation or coaching suggestion
Include uncertainty (e.g. "I'm not sure how much it matters for training decisions")
Never include links unless explicitly asked

quality_checklist: Mention pattern matches the approved Reddit-safe framing (single mention, then pronouns)
No praise/superlative language beyond what the source material itself states
Tone is factual and uncertain, not promotional
source: KORR_Reddit_Skill.pdf ("Reddit-Safe KORR Framing" section), provided directly by user, 2026-08-07
